justification: Assessment returned INVALID at step 0040 and its stated defect is the same one as ground truth: the zero-exponent case is not actually discharged because phi(x)=x^(q/p) fails to be a usable real function there. It explicitly states 'phi = x^{q/p} is either undefined for p = 0 or constant for q = 0, giving the vacuous 1 <= 1 and an undefined exponent 1/q', which is exactly the ground-truth flaw (p=0 makes q/p=1/0 undefined, so phi is not defined and Jensen cannot be applied). Its primary witness (p=-1,q=0,x=(1,2)) is a different-but-valid instance of the same claim (phi constant, 1/q undefined, no comparison obtainable), and it also names the p=0 undefined-exponent branch directly. Rephrasing plus a different valid witness for the same claim counts as matching.
